newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds out-manoeuvre US, bill strip firm.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds out-manoeuvre US, bill strip firm.

text.p: *Australian bonds put in a strong outperformance against the U.S. as the market continued to accept that Australia should not fear a further tightening by the Federal Reserve.
*Bill futures firm, June contract back in line with cassh.

Australian bonds put in a strong outperformance against the U.S. as the market continued to accept that Australia should not fear a further tightening by the Federal Reserve based on local fundamentals, traders said.

Bond futures surged in early trading as the market repriced itself against U.S. Treasuries taking the Australia/U.S. 10-year down to around 94 basis points at one stage, it lowest level since mid-February, and a move that caught people short.
Bill futures also rallied, taking the June contract to 94.00 and back in line with 6.0 percent official cash rates, having been discounting a 1/4 point tightening just over a month ago.
Further forward bill contracts were also firm as expectations of a tightening by the RBA were pushed further out.
"The continued realisation that we are not going to follow the Fed is keeping the bills perky," said one short-end trader.
"The recent volatility of equites and bonds is also seeing some funds moving to cash, i.e. bills, which is leaving the market short," he added.

The outperformance against the U.S. has gathered pace since last week's weak labour force report, which has prompted some speculation that the RBA could ease again if key local data over the next few weeks proves subdued.

The March quarter CPI is due next week and average weekly earnings are due on May 1, and the market is still awaiting a verdict on the "living wage" claim by the Australian Industrial Relations Committee.
Meanwhile, the U.S. releases its March CPI later on Tuesday and close attention will be paid to the core rate after the 0.4 percent jump in the PPI core rate seen last Friday.
U.S. Treasury prices continued to slip in early Tokyo trading ahead of the data having shown modest falls in New York on Monday.

The local rally also saw an outperformance against Canadian debt, which had shown modest resistance to the U.S. on Monday. However, N.Z. bonds outshone the bloc following much weaker than expected March quarter inflation. The RBNZ said underlying inflation was 0.22 percent against a forecast 0.5 percent.
